expectations.text: Does NOT simply endorse switching to 2PL because the LRT and AIC favor it
expectations.evidence: Your professor isn't being stubborn — she's defending a substantive position, and the LRT doesn't actually win the argument you think it does.

expectations.text: Explains that Rasch vs. 2PL is a measurement philosophy choice, not a fit competition: Rasch commits to specific objectivity — person parameters are invariant across item subsets and item parameters are invariant across person subsamples
expectations.evidence: Equal discrimination across items isn't just a statistical convenience — it's the precondition for specific objectivity: the property that person parameters (reading ability estimates) are invariant across which subset of items you use, and item parameters are invariant across which subsample of persons you draw.

expectations.text: Explains what the LRT result actually means: items have unequal discriminations, which violates the Rasch assumption — but this is a finding about the items, not necessarily a reason to abandon the model
expectations.evidence: In plain language: your 30 items do not all discriminate equally well... That is a finding about your items, not a verdict on your measurement model.

expectations.text: Names the Rasch response to misfit: items that do not fit the model are candidates for revision or removal, not a reason to switch models — the model defines the measurement target
expectations.evidence: The Rasch response is not 'switch models' — it's 'investigate and revise.' Items with very low discrimination may be poorly written, ambiguous, or measuring a tangential sub-skill... Both are candidates for revision or removal.

expectations.text: States that accepting 2PL (variable discriminations) means accepting that different items carry different weight in measuring the construct, which has implications for score comparability and test generalizability
expectations.evidence: Switching to 2PL means accepting variable item weights in measuring the construct... Score generalizability is reduced. If you swap out high-discrimination items for similar-content replacements in a future form, your theta scale shifts unless you re-equate carefully.

expectations.text: Does not declare Rasch definitively superior — acknowledges this is a genuine philosophical debate — but holds that the LRT alone does not resolve it in favor of 2PL
expectations.evidence: This isn't a case where one side is obviously right. The Rasch position is defensible and your professor is not wrong to prefer it. The Birnbaum position is also defensible... The LRT says the data are inconsistent with equal discriminations. It does not say 'abandon Rasch.'
